metadata.title: Product Experiences
metadata.description: Outcome-based product capabilities for the Enterprise Architecture Management Platform domain.

definitions.productBrick: A reusable implementation-facing building block used to realize one or more product experiences.
definitions.productCapability: A high-level, outcome-based experience that delivers customer or business value.

rootGroups.name: Architecture and Transformation Journeys
rootGroups.description: Outcome-oriented experiences that connect architecture evidence to business and technology decisions.

capabilities.name: Build a Living Enterprise Blueprint
capabilities.description: Create a continuously updated model of capabilities, applications, technologies, processes, data, people, and dependencies.
outcomes: Faster time to decision-ready enterprise visibility

flows.title: Build a Living Enterprise Blueprint
flows.description: Move from static diagrams and fragmented inventories to a governed, living architecture knowledge graph.

steps.title: Define the model
keyFacts: Enterprise architecture teams need a metamodel that fits their operating model without creating a bespoke product fork.
painPoints: Rigid models force teams back into spreadsheets and disconnected diagrams.

dependencies.name: Configurable Metamodel Studio
dependencies.description: Defines object types, relationship rules, attributes, and validation policies.
dependencies.how: Creates the common language for architecture content.

dependencies.name: Architecture Repository
dependencies.description: Stores governed architecture objects and relationships.
dependencies.how: Provides the durable source of truth.

steps.title: Populate and sync
keyFacts: Initial value depends on quickly importing existing inventories and keeping source data fresh.
painPoints: Architecture models lose trust when they are stale after the first workshop.

dependencies.name: Bulk Import and Mapping Workbench
dependencies.description: Maps existing spreadsheets and exports into the model.
dependencies.how: Reduces migration effort from existing EA and portfolio artifacts.

dependencies.name: Source System Synchronization
dependencies.description: Keeps operational sources synchronized.

steps.title: Validate and use
keyFacts: Architecture content becomes valuable when it connects business capabilities, applications, technologies, and processes.
painPoints: Executive teams reject architecture outputs when they cannot trace the insight to trusted objects.

dependencies.name: Business Capability Model
dependencies.description: Connects business language to technology evidence.
dependencies.how: Makes the blueprint meaningful to non-architects.

dependencies.name: Application Portfolio Catalog
dependencies.description: Adds application context for portfolio decisions.
dependencies.how: Connects the blueprint to investment and risk decisions.

externalSystemsThisCapabilityDependsOn.system: Customer CMDB, spreadsheets, SPM, identity, and IT asset systems
externalSystemsThisCapabilityDependsOn.interface: file import, APIs, SSO, and scheduled sync
externalSystemsThisCapabilityDependsOn.description: Provide source records and ownership context for initial architecture population and ongoing freshness.

capabilities.name: Rationalize the Application Portfolio
capabilities.description: Identify redundant, risky, costly, or low-value applications and convert analysis into defensible modernization and retirement decisions.
outcomes: Reduced application spend and technical debt
Clear investment decisions backed by cost, risk, usage, and dependency evidence

flows.title: Rationalize the Application Portfolio
flows.description: Move from fragmented application lists to an agreed investment, modernization, and retirement plan.

steps.title: Segment portfolio
keyFacts: Portfolio leaders need application context by capability, owner, cost, lifecycle, and criticality.
painPoints: Rationalization efforts stall when each team argues from a different application list.

dependencies.name: Application Portfolio Catalog
dependencies.description: Provides canonical application records.
dependencies.how: Creates the shared baseline for assessment.

steps.title: Score decisions
keyFacts: Rationalization recommendations must combine value, cost, risk, lifecycle, and dependency evidence.
painPoints: Cost-only analysis produces retirement recommendations that are unsafe or politically impossible.

dependencies.name: Application Rationalization Engine
dependencies.description: Creates investment, tolerate, migrate, and retire recommendations.

dependencies.name: Risk and Criticality Scoring
dependencies.description: Adds business and operational risk context.

steps.title: Commit plan
keyFacts: Executive teams need the decision package, not just a dashboard.
painPoints: Application retirement lists fail without owner alignment and measurable value tracking.

dependencies.name: Executive Dashboards and Presentations
dependencies.description: Packages recommendations for leadership review.

externalSystemsThisCapabilityDependsOn.system: CMDB, SaaS management, procurement, finance, and security systems
externalSystemsThisCapabilityDependsOn.description: Supply portfolio, cost, usage, lifecycle, and risk signals.

capabilities.name: Plan Transformation Roadmaps
capabilities.description: Translate strategy and capability gaps into architecture roadmaps, target states, investment sequencing, and transformation milestones.
outcomes: Better alignment between strategy, architecture, funding, and delivery

flows.title: Plan Transformation Roadmaps
flows.description: Create sequenced roadmap options that connect strategic goals to target architecture and funded change.

steps.title: Connect strategy
keyFacts: Transformation leaders need a shared capability map before prioritizing initiatives.
painPoints: Strategy decks do not reveal which applications, technologies, and teams must change.

dependencies.name: Business Capability Model
dependencies.description: Connects strategic themes to capabilities and current-state gaps.
dependencies.how: Provides the business structure for roadmap planning.

steps.title: Model options
keyFacts: Roadmaps need scenario comparison across cost, value, risk, dependency, and timing.
painPoints: Single-plan roadmaps hide tradeoffs and create late-stage surprises.

dependencies.name: Scenario Simulation Engine
dependencies.description: Compares baseline and future-state options.

dependencies.name: Target State Roadmapping
dependencies.description: Stores the selected target states and milestones.
dependencies.how: Turns scenario choices into a roadmap.

steps.title: Align funding
keyFacts: Funded transformation portfolios need architecture evidence linked to benefits and execution work.
painPoints: Portfolio decisions are hard to defend when expected benefits are not connected to affected capabilities and applications.

dependencies.name: Strategic Portfolio Fit
dependencies.description: Scores initiative fit against architecture and strategy.

dependencies.name: Value Realization Tracker
dependencies.description: Tracks expected and realized outcome value.

externalSystemsThisCapabilityDependsOn.system: OKR, SPM, finance, agile planning, and project portfolio systems
externalSystemsThisCapabilityDependsOn.description: Provide strategic goals, budgets, initiatives, and delivery state.

capabilities.name: Assess Change Impact
capabilities.description: Explain the blast radius of proposed application, technology, process, data, supplier, or AI changes before teams commit.

flows.title: Assess Change Impact
flows.description: Use graph evidence to show affected capabilities, systems, data, processes, teams, controls, and roadmap commitments.

steps.title: Select change
keyFacts: The same impact engine must support planned roadmap changes, urgent risk issues, and solution designs.
painPoints: Impact assessment is slow when analysts manually chase owners and diagrams.

dependencies.name: Solution Design Workspace
dependencies.description: Captures the proposed change and design context.

steps.title: Run impact
keyFacts: Relationship depth, confidence, and risk scores determine whether the impact result is trusted.
painPoints: Stakeholders ignore impact output when it cannot explain why an item is affected.

dependencies.name: Dependency Map Analytics
dependencies.description: Traverses dependencies and relationship paths.

dependencies.name: Change Impact Analyzer
dependencies.description: Packages and explains impact findings.
dependencies.how: Turns graph traversal into decision evidence.

steps.title: Communicate risk
keyFacts: Architecture impact must be communicated in business terms for governance forums.
painPoints: Review boards become bottlenecks when impact findings stay technical and unresolved.

dependencies.name: Executive Dashboards and Presentations
dependencies.description: Presents impact findings for stakeholders.

externalSystemsThisCapabilityDependsOn.system: Change, delivery, security, and portfolio systems
externalSystemsThisCapabilityDependsOn.description: Provide change context and receive impact evidence.

capabilities.name: Govern Technology Risk and Standards
capabilities.description: Manage technology standards, lifecycle exposure, policy exceptions, controls, and audit evidence across the enterprise architecture model.
outcomes: Faster evidence collection for audits and regulatory reviews

flows.title: Govern Technology Risk and Standards
flows.description: Connect standards and controls to the systems, capabilities, and decisions they govern.

steps.title: Map standards
keyFacts: Technology standards are actionable only when mapped to real applications and ownership.
painPoints: Standards catalogs drift when they are separate from the architecture repository.

dependencies.name: Technology Portfolio and Standards
dependencies.description: Stores approved, tolerated, contained, and prohibited technologies.

steps.title: Evaluate controls
keyFacts: Regulated enterprises need control traceability across systems, AI, data, and delivery decisions.
painPoints: Audit readiness is expensive when control evidence is recreated for each review.

dependencies.name: Controls and Compliance Mapping
dependencies.description: Maps controls to architecture objects and decisions.

dependencies.name: Audit Trail and Evidence Vault
dependencies.description: Preserves evidence packages.

steps.title: Manage exceptions
keyFacts: Exception handling needs accountable owners, expiry dates, and compensating controls.
painPoints: Risk grows silently when architecture exceptions are approved but never revisited.

dependencies.name: Governance Policy Engine
dependencies.description: Routes review and exception decisions.

externalSystemsThisCapabilityDependsOn.system: GRC, vulnerability management, ITSM, CMDB, and audit systems
externalSystemsThisCapabilityDependsOn.description: Provide risk, control, lifecycle, and audit requirements.

capabilities.name: Engage Business Stakeholders
capabilities.description: Invite business and IT stakeholders to validate data, review decisions, consume insight, and contribute to architecture outcomes without requiring expert modeling skills.
outcomes: Broader use of architecture evidence in business decisions

flows.title: Engage Business Stakeholders
flows.description: Turn enterprise architecture from an expert repository into an operating rhythm for business and technology stakeholders.

steps.title: Invite contributors
keyFacts: Most architecture data lives with owners outside the architecture team.
painPoints: Expert-only tools create a bottleneck and stale content.

dependencies.name: Stakeholder Survey and Data Collection
dependencies.description: Captures ownership validation and data updates.

steps.title: Route work
keyFacts: Stakeholder tasks must be scoped, permissioned, and tracked to completion.
painPoints: Data collection campaigns fail when owners cannot see what is expected of them.

dependencies.name: Architecture Work Queue
dependencies.description: Routes data quality, review, and governance work.
dependencies.how: Turns architecture improvement into accountable work.

steps.title: Share insight
keyFacts: Business stakeholders need role-specific dashboards and plain-language explanations.
painPoints: Architecture insight is ignored when it appears as raw diagrams or specialist notation only.

dependencies.name: Executive Dashboards and Presentations
dependencies.description: Delivers role-based decision views.
dependencies.how: Makes architecture evidence useful outside the architecture team.

dependencies.name: AI Architecture Insight Assistant
dependencies.description: Summarizes and explains evidence.

externalSystemsThisCapabilityDependsOn.system: Identity, email, Teams, Slack, and executive reporting tools
externalSystemsThisCapabilityDependsOn.description: Reach stakeholders where they already work.

capabilities.name: Integrate Architecture Operating Data
capabilities.description: Connect architecture models to operational systems so data quality, freshness, and source lineage can be governed over time.

flows.title: Integrate Architecture Operating Data
flows.description: Create trustworthy pipelines from operational systems into the architecture model.

steps.title: Connect sources
keyFacts: Architecture data comes from many systems with different owners and quality levels.
painPoints: Manual imports cannot keep up with fast-changing application and technology estates.

dependencies.name: Source System Synchronization
dependencies.description: Runs connector syncs and preserves source lineage.

steps.title: Map and validate
keyFacts: Data mapping must be visible and correctable by architecture administrators.
painPoints: Silent mapping errors create false confidence in dashboards and impact analysis.

dependencies.name: Bulk Import and Mapping Workbench
dependencies.description: Maps source data into the metamodel.

dependencies.name: Architecture Data Quality Monitor
dependencies.description: Scores freshness, completeness, and confidence.
dependencies.how: Identifies quality gaps before users rely on the data.

steps.title: Operate freshness
keyFacts: Data freshness needs operational monitoring, not one-time migration validation.
painPoints: Architecture trust erodes when source syncs fail silently.

dependencies.name: Architecture Repository
dependencies.description: Maintains the current architecture graph.

externalSystemsThisCapabilityDependsOn.system: ITSM, CMDB, cloud, SPM, security, HR, finance, and procurement systems
externalSystemsThisCapabilityDependsOn.interface: REST APIs, webhooks, file imports, and secure connectors
externalSystemsThisCapabilityDependsOn.description: Provide operating data used for architecture insight.

capabilities.name: Prove AI-Ready Architecture Governance
capabilities.description: Use architecture evidence to discover, classify, govern, and monitor AI systems, AI agents, data dependencies, controls, risks, and business value.
outcomes: Safer adoption of AI systems and agents across business capabilities

flows.title: Prove AI-Ready Architecture Governance
flows.description: Connect AI use cases, agents, data dependencies, owners, controls, risks, and value outcomes to the enterprise architecture model.

steps.title: Discover AI landscape
keyFacts: AI adoption creates new dependencies between agents, applications, data, controls, and business capabilities.
painPoints: AI inventories become stale quickly if they are separate from operating architecture data.

dependencies.name: AI Architecture Insight Assistant
dependencies.description: Assists with classification, summaries, and insight generation.

dependencies.name: Business Capability Model
dependencies.description: Maps AI systems to business capabilities.
dependencies.how: Connects AI governance to business value.

steps.title: Attach controls
keyFacts: AI governance requires evidence of ownership, data use, model risk, controls, and decision authority.
painPoints: Policy teams cannot govern AI systems that are not connected to applications, data, and capabilities.

dependencies.name: Controls and Compliance Mapping
dependencies.description: Maps control obligations to AI and architecture objects.

dependencies.name: Risk and Criticality Scoring
dependencies.description: Scores risk and criticality.

steps.title: Report readiness
keyFacts: Executives need AI adoption status, risk exposure, control gaps, and business value in one view.
painPoints: AI governance becomes a blocker when stakeholders see only risk without value or roadmap context.

dependencies.name: Executive Dashboards and Presentations
dependencies.description: Delivers AI governance readiness reporting.
dependencies.how: Makes AI adoption and risk visible to leadership.

externalSystemsThisCapabilityDependsOn.system: AI registries, model gateways, data catalogs, GRC platforms, and security systems
externalSystemsThisCapabilityDependsOn.description: Provide AI system, data, risk, and control evidence.
